input.quote: 7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
input.rationale: § 7.6 imposes USD 25,000 per day in liquidated damages on Customer for any dependency delay, with no cure period, materiality threshold, or aggregate cap. That is a penalty running against us and is worse than both the preferred (no Customer-payable liquidated damages) and the fallback (a single early-termination fee capped at three months' fees), and the § 21.1 mutual cap does not neutralise a per-day accrual triggered by minor delays. It is the only liquidated-damages or penalty mechanic in the document, so we take the preferred position and replace the per-day formula with an express statement that Customer owes no liquidated damages or penalties; Vendor retains its ordinary capped damages remedies and nothing else cross-references § 7.6.

mappings.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.

proposal.summary: Remove the USD 25,000 per day Customer-payable liquidated damages in § 7.6 and state that Customer owes no liquidated damages or penalties.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We deleted the USD 25,000 per day liquidated damages running against us for dependency delays; our position is that Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties, with Vendor left to its actual, capped damages. If a liquidated amount is unavoidable, we can accept only an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.

ops.oldText: Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
ops.newText: Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages or penalties under this Agreement.
